verses.zh: 以法莲人对基甸说：「你去与米甸人争战，没有招我们同去，为甚么这样待我们呢？」他们就与基甸大大地争吵。
verses.en: The Ephraimites said to him, “Why have you done such a thing to us? You did not summon us[NOTE:1] when you went to fight the Midianites!” They argued vehemently with him.
notes: Heb “by not summoning us.”

verses.zh: 基甸对他们说：「我所行的岂能比你们所行的呢？以法莲拾取剩下的葡萄不强过亚比以谢所摘的葡萄吗？
verses.en: He said to them, “Now what have I accomplished compared to you? Even Ephraim’s leftover grapes[NOTE:1] are better quality than Abiezer’s harvest![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “gleanings.”

Ephraim’s leftover grapes are better quality than Abiezer’s harvest. Gideon employs an agricultural metaphor. He argues that Ephraim’s mopping up operations, though seemingly like the inferior grapes which are missed initially by the harvesters or left for the poor, are actually more noteworthy than the military efforts of Gideon’s family.

verses.zh: 神已将米甸人的两个首领俄立和西伊伯交在你们手中；我所行的岂能比你们所行的呢？」基甸说了这话，以法莲人的怒气就消了。
verses.en: It was to you that God handed over the Midianite generals, Oreb and Zeeb! What did I accomplish to rival that?”[NOTE:1] When he said this, they calmed down.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “What was I able to do compared to you?”
Heb “Then their spirits relaxed from against him, when he spoke this word.”

verses.zh: 基甸和跟随他的三百人到约旦河过渡，虽然疲乏，还是追赶。
verses.en: Now Gideon and his 300 men had crossed over the Jordan River, and even though they were exhausted, they were still chasing the Midianites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And Gideon arrived at the Jordan, crossing over, he and the 300 men who were with him, exhausted and chasing.” The English past perfect (“had crossed”) is used because this verse flashes back chronologically to an event that preceded the hostile encounter described in vv. 1-3. (Note that 7:25 assumes Gideon had already crossed the Jordan.)

verses.zh: 基甸对疏割人说：「求你们拿饼来给跟随我的人吃，因为他们疲乏了；我们追赶米甸人的两个王西巴和撒慕拿。」
verses.en: He said to the men of Sukkoth, “Give[NOTE:1] some loaves of bread to the men[NOTE:2] who are following me[NOTE:3] because they are exhausted. I am chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
notes: Or perhaps, “sell.”
Heb “people.” The translation uses “men” because these were warriors and in ancient Israelite culture would have been exclusively males.
Heb “who are at my feet.”

verses.zh: 疏割人的首领回答说：「西巴和撒慕拿已经在你手里，你使我们将饼给你的军兵吗？」
verses.en: The officials of Sukkoth said, “You have not yet overpowered Zebah and Zalmunna. So why should we give[NOTE:1] bread to your army?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or perhaps, “sell.”

Heb “Are the palms of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give to your army bread?” Perhaps the reference to the kings’ “palms” should be taken literally. The officials of Sukkoth may be alluding to the practice of mutilating prisoners or enemy corpses (see R. G. Boling, Judges [AB], 155).sn The officials of Sukkoth are hesitant to give (or sell) food to Gideon’s forces because they are not sure of the outcome of the battle. Perhaps they had made an alliance with the Midianites which demanded their loyalty.

verses.zh: 基甸说：「耶和华将西巴和撒慕拿交在我手之后，我就用野地的荆条和枳棘打伤你们。」
verses.en: Gideon said, “Since you will not help,[NOTE:1] after the Lord hands Zebah and Zalmunna over to me, I will thresh[NOTE:2] your skin[NOTE:3] with[NOTE:4] desert thorns and briers.”
notes: Heb “Therefore.”

I will thresh. The metaphor is agricultural. Threshing was usually done on a hard threshing floor. As farm animals walked over the stalks, pulling behind them a board embedded with sharp stones, the stalks and grain would be separated. See O. Borowski, Agriculture in Iron Age Israel, 63-65. Gideon threatens to use thorns and briers on his sledge.
Or “flesh.”

This is apparently a rare instrumental use of the Hebrew preposition אֵת (ʾet, note the use of ב [bet] in v. 16). Some, however, argue that אֵת more naturally indicates accompaniment (“together with”). In this case Gideon envisions threshing their skin along with thorns and briers, just as the stalks and grain are intermingled on the threshing floor. See C. F. Burney, Judges, 229-30.

verses.zh: 基甸从那里上到毗努伊勒，对那里的人也是这样说；毗努伊勒人也与疏割人回答他的话一样。
verses.en: He went up from there to Penuel and made the same request.[NOTE:1] The men of Penuel responded the same way the men of Sukkoth had.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and spoke to them in the same way.”
Heb “The men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Sukkoth answered.”

verses.zh: 他向毗努伊勒人说：「我平平安安回来的时候，我必拆毁这楼。」
verses.en: He also threatened[NOTE:1] the men of Penuel, warning,[NOTE:2] “When I return victoriously,[NOTE:3] I will tear down this tower.”
notes: Heb “said to.” The translation “threatened” is interpretive, but is clearly indicated by the context.
Heb “saying.”
Or “safely.” Heb “in peace.”

verses.zh: 那时西巴和撒慕拿，并跟随他们的军队都在加各，约有一万五千人，就是东方人全军所剩下的；已经被杀约有十二万拿刀的。
verses.en: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their armies. There were about 15,000 survivors from the army of the eastern peoples; 120,000 sword-wielding soldiers had been killed.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “About 15,000 [in number] were all the ones remaining from the army of the sons of the east. The fallen ones were 120,000 [in number], men drawing the sword.”

verses.zh: 基甸就由挪巴和约比哈东边，从住帐棚人的路上去，杀败了米甸人的军兵，因为他们坦然无惧。
verses.en: Gideon went up the road of the nomads[NOTE:1] east of Nobah and Jogbehah and ambushed the surprised army.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the ones living in tents.”

Heb “and attacked the army, while the army was secure.” The Hebrew term בֶטַח (vetakh, “secure”) may means the army was undefended (see R. G. Boling, Judges [AB], 156), not suspecting an attack at that time and place. A few mss supported by the LXX read the participle form from the same root, בֹטֵחַ (voteakh) “trustingly,” the implication being that they were not attentive to defense.

verses.zh: 西巴和撒慕拿逃跑；基甸追赶他们，捉住米甸的二王西巴和撒慕拿，惊散全军。
verses.en: When Zebah and Zalmunna ran away, Gideon[NOTE:1] chased them and captured the two Midianite kings, Zebah and Zalmunna. He had surprised[NOTE:2] their entire army.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Gideon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “routed”; Heb “caused to panic.”

verses.zh: 约阿施的儿子基甸由希列斯坡从阵上回来，
verses.en: Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the pass[NOTE:1] of Heres.
notes: Or “ascent.”

verses.zh: 捉住疏割的一个少年人，问他：「疏割的首领长老是谁？」他就将首领长老七十七个人的名字写出来。
verses.en: He captured a young man from Sukkoth[NOTE:1] and interrogated him. The young man wrote down for him the names of Sukkoth’s officials and city leaders—77 men in all.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from the men of Sukkoth.”
Heb “wrote down for him the officials of Sukkoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.”

verses.zh: 基甸到了疏割，对那里的人说：「你们从前讥诮我说：『西巴和撒慕拿已经在你手里，你使我们将饼给跟随你的疲乏人吗？』现在西巴和撒慕拿在这里。」
verses.en: He approached the men of Sukkoth and said, “Look what I have![NOTE:1] Zebah and Zalmunna! You insulted me, saying, ‘You have not yet overpowered Zebah and Zalmunna. So why should we give bread to your exhausted men?’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Look!” The words “what I have” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

Heb “Are the palms of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give to your exhausted men bread?” sn Gideon changes their actual statement (see v. 6) by saying exhausted men rather than “army.” In this way he emphasizes the crisis his men were facing and highlights the insensitivity of the men of Sukkoth.

verses.zh: 于是捉住那城内的长老，用野地的荆条和枳棘责打（原文是指教）疏割人；
verses.en: He seized the leaders[NOTE:1] of the city, along with some desert thorns and briers; he then “threshed” the men of Sukkoth with them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “elders.”

The translation follows the reading of several ancient versions (LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate) in assuming the form וַיָּדָשׁ (vayyadash) from the verb דּוּשׁ (dush, “thresh”) as in v. 7. The MT reads instead the form וַיֹּדַע (vayyodaʿ, “make known”), a Hiphil form of יָדַע (yadaʿ). In this case one could translate, “he used them [i.e., the thorns and briers] to teach the men of Sukkoth a lesson.”

verses.zh: 又拆了毗努伊勒的楼，杀了那城里的人。
verses.en: He also tore down the tower of Penuel and executed the city’s men.

verses.zh: 基甸问西巴和撒慕拿说：「你们在他泊山所杀的人是甚么样式？」回答说：「他们好像你，各人都有王子的样式。」
verses.en: He said to Zebah and Zalmunna, “Describe for me[NOTE:1] the men you killed at Tabor.” They said, “They were like you. Each one looked like a king’s son.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Where are?”
Heb “each one like the appearance of sons of the king.”

verses.zh: 基甸说：「他们是我同母的弟兄，我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你们从前若存留他们的性命，我如今就不杀你们了。」
verses.en: He said, “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. I swear,[NOTE:1] as surely as the Lord is alive, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”
notes: The words “I swear” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 于是对他的长子益帖说：「你起来杀他们。」但益帖因为是童子，害怕，不敢拔刀。
verses.en: He ordered Jether his firstborn son, “Come on![NOTE:1] Kill them!” But Jether was too afraid to draw his sword[NOTE:2] because he was still young.
notes: Or “Arise!”
Heb “did not draw his sword for he was afraid.”

verses.zh: 西巴和撒慕拿说：「你自己起来杀我们吧！因为人如何，力量也是如何。」基甸就起来，杀了西巴和撒慕拿，夺获他们骆驼项上戴的月牙圈。
verses.en: Zebah and Zalmunna said to Gideon,[NOTE:1] “Come on,[NOTE:2] you strike us, for a man is judged by his strength.”[NOTE:3] So Gideon killed[NOTE:4] Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent-shaped ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.
notes: The words “to Gideon” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Or “Arise.”
Heb “for as the man is his strength.”
Heb “arose and killed.”

verses.zh: 以色列人对基甸说：「你既救我们脱离米甸人的手，愿你和你的儿孙管理我们。」
verses.en: The men of Israel said to Gideon, “Rule over us—you, your son, and your grandson. For you have delivered us from Midian’s power.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “hand.”

verses.zh: 基甸说：「我不管理你们，我的儿子也不管理你们，惟有耶和华管理你们。」
verses.en: Gideon said to them, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son rule over you. The Lord will rule over you.”

verses.zh: 基甸又对他们说：「我有一件事求你们：请你们各人将所夺的耳环给我。」（原来仇敌是以实玛利人，都是戴金耳环的。）
verses.en: Gideon continued,[NOTE:1] “I would like to make one request. Each of you give me an earring from the plunder you have taken.”[NOTE:2] (The Midianites[NOTE:3] had gold earrings because they were Ishmaelites.)
notes: Heb “said to them.”
Heb “Give to me, each one, an earring from his plunder.”
Heb “they”; the referent (the Midianites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他们说：「我们情愿给你」，就铺开一件外衣，各人将所夺的耳环丢在其上。
verses.en: They said, “We are happy to give you earrings.”[NOTE:1] So they[NOTE:2] spread out a garment, and each one threw an earring from his plunder onto it.
notes: Heb “We will indeed give.”
In the LXX the subject of this verb is singular, referring to Gideon rather than to the Israelites.

verses.zh: 基甸所要出来的金耳环重一千七百舍客勒金子。此外还有米甸王所戴的月环、耳坠，和所穿的紫色衣服，并骆驼项上的金链子。
verses.en: The total weight of the gold earrings he requested came to 1,700 gold shekels.[NOTE:1] This was in addition to the crescent-shaped ornaments, jewelry,[NOTE:2] purple clothing worn by the Midianite kings, and the necklaces on the camels.[NOTE:3]
notes: 1,700 gold shekels would be about 42.7 pounds (19.4 kilograms) of gold.
Or “pendants.”
Heb “the ornaments which were on the necks of their camels.”

verses.zh: 基甸以此制造了一个以弗得，设立在本城俄弗拉。后来以色列人拜那以弗得行了邪淫；这就作了基甸和他全家的网罗。
verses.en: Gideon used all this to make[NOTE:1] an ephod,[NOTE:2] which he put in his hometown of Ophrah. All the Israelites[NOTE:3] prostituted themselves to it by worshiping it[NOTE:4] there. It became a snare to Gideon and his family.
notes: Heb “made it into.”

In Exod 28:4-6 and several other texts an ephod is described as a priestly or cultic garment. In some cases an ephod is used to obtain a divine oracle (1 Sam 23:9; 30:7). Here the ephod is made of gold and is described as being quite heavy (70-75 lbs?). Some identify it as an idol, but it was more likely a cultic object fashioned in the form of a garment which was used for oracular purposes. For discussion of the ephod in the OT, see C. F. Burney, Judges, 236-43, and R. de Vaux, Ancient Israel, 349-52.
Heb “Israel” (a collective singular).
The words “by worshiping it” are supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 这样，米甸人被以色列人制伏了，不敢再抬头。基甸还在的日子，国中太平四十年。
verses.en: The Israelites humiliated Midian; the Midianites’ fighting spirit was broken.[NOTE:1] The land had rest for 40 years during Gideon’s time.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Midian was humbled before the Israelites, and they no longer lifted their heads.”
Heb “in the days of Gideon.”

verses.zh: 约阿施的儿子耶路・巴力回去，住在自己家里。
verses.en: Then Jerub Baal son of Joash went home and settled down.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “went and lived in his house.”

verses.zh: 基甸有七十个亲生的儿子，因为他有许多的妻。
verses.en: Gideon fathered 70 sons through his many wives.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Gideon had 70 sons who went out from his thigh, for he had many wives.” The Hebrew word יָרֵךְ (yarekh, “thigh”) is a euphemism here for the penis.

verses.zh: 他的妾住在示剑，也给他生了一个儿子。基甸与他起名叫亚比米勒。
verses.en: His concubine,[NOTE:1] who lived in Shechem, also gave him a son, whom he named Abimelech.[NOTE:2]
notes: A concubine was a slave woman in ancient Near Eastern societies who was the legal property of her master, but who could have legitimate sexual relations with her master. A concubine’s status was more elevated than a mere servant, but she was not free and did not have the legal rights of a free wife. The children of a concubine could, in some instances, become equal heirs with the children of the free wife. After the period of the Judges concubines may have become more of a royal prerogative (2 Sam 21:10-14; 1 Kgs 11:3).
The name Abimelech means “my father is king.”

verses.zh: 约阿施的儿子基甸，年纪老迈而死，葬在亚比以谢族的俄弗拉，在他父亲约阿施的坟墓里。
verses.en: Gideon son of Joash died at a very[NOTE:1] old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash located in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
notes: Heb “good.”

verses.zh: 基甸死后，以色列人又去随从诸巴力行邪淫，以巴力・比利土为他们的神。
verses.en: After Gideon died, the Israelites again prostituted themselves to the Baals. They made Baal Berith[NOTE:1] their god.
notes: Baal Berith was a local manifestation of the Canaanite storm god. The name means, ironically, “Baal of the covenant.” Israel’s covenant allegiance had indeed shifted.

verses.zh: 以色列人不记念耶和华―他们的　神，就是拯救他们脱离四围仇敌之手的，
verses.en: The Israelites did not remain true[NOTE:1] to the Lord their God, who had delivered them from all the enemies who lived around them.
notes: Heb “remember.”

verses.zh: 也不照着耶路・巴力，就是基甸向他们所施的恩惠厚待他的家。
verses.en: They did not treat[NOTE:1] the family of Jerub Baal (that is, Gideon) fairly in return for all the good he had done for Israel.
notes: Heb “did not do loyalty with,” or “did not act faithfully toward.”
